explanation: A broad dial for running parallel structure: it rises on the separators and items of a punctuated series of short like-kind units (comma-, equals- or 'then'-separated numbers, indexed variables like x_1, x_2, repeated HTML tags, LaTeX braces) and on byte pieces of Devanagari/Arabic script, crossing a quarter of max by the third item or within 3-6 tokens of such script even in very short texts, and reaching 0.4-0.7 of max on the third and later items. Plain prose in any Latin-script language sits at 0.1-0.25 of max when under about 14 tokens and only creeps to 0.25-0.35 in longer passages; text that opens with a run of bare space-separated words or numbers with no punctuation or function words (e.g. 'cat dog cow pig', 'Paris London Rome', 'one two three') stays at exactly 0 however long it is, and the first token and sentence-final periods are always 0.
